item.title: BE ALERT - SQUALL WATCH IN EFFECT
item.description:
Windstorm Warning | Squall Watch In Effect |

Showers and thunderstorms are expected to track east across the region after midnight. Some of these storms could produce squalls with wind gusts up to 45 knots and hail up to 2 cm in diameter. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. For more information monitor Canadian Coast Guard radio or Weatheradio stations.

| Extreme - extraordinary threat | Expected - act within an hour

item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - SEVERE THUNDERSTORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Thunderstorm/Lightning Warning | Yellow Warning - Severe Thunderstorm - In Effect |

At 10:05 p.m. CDT, a line of severe thunderstorms is located from Dugald to Ile des Chênes. These severe thunderstorms are moving east at 30 km/h. Strong wind gusts, up to quarter size hail and heavy rain are possible. Locations and nearby areas that could be impacted include: Grande Pointe, Ile des Chênes, Oakbank, Dugald, Landmark, Anola, La Coulée, Ste-Geneviève Severe thunderstorm warnings are issued when imminent or occurring thunderstorms are expected to produce damaging hail, wind or rain.

| Moderate - possible threat | Immediate - act now | Tyndall, Manitoba

item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - SEVERE THUNDERSTORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Thunderstorm/Lightning Warning | Yellow Warning - Severe Thunderstorm - In Effect |

At 10:02 p.m. CDT, a severe thunderstorm is located about 20 km northeast of Aikens Lake. This severe thunderstorm is moving east at 45 km/h. Damaging wind gusts, loonie to ping pong ball size hail and heavy rain are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, soft shelters or trees is likely. Large hail may cause significant damage and injury. Severe thunderstorm warnings are issued when imminent or occurring thunderstorms are expected to produce damaging hail, wind or rain.

| Moderate - possible threat | Immediate - act now

item.title: BE ALERT - SQUALL WATCH IN EFFECT
item.description:
Windstorm Warning | Squall Watch In Effect |

A trough of low pressure moving across southern Manitoba this evening may produce severe thunderstorms. What: wind gusts up to 60 knots. Up to ping-pong ball-sized hail. Large hail can damage vessels and cause injury. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. For more information monitor Canadian Coast Guard radio or Weatheradio stations.

| Extreme - extraordinary threat | Expected - act within an hour

item.title: BE ALERT - ORANGE WATCH - SEVERE THUNDERSTORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Thunderstorm/Lightning Warning | Orange Watch - Severe Thunderstorm - In Effect |

Conditions are favourable for the development of dangerous thunderstorms that may be capable of producing strong wind gusts, damaging hail and heavy rain. A trough of low pressure moving across southern Manitoba this evening may cause severe thunderstorms to develop. What: wind gusts up to 110 km/h. Up to ping pong sized hail. Locally heavy rain. Additional information: a isolated tornado threat is also possible with any storm that develops. Severe thunderstorm watches are issued when conditions are favourable for the development of thunderstorms capable of producing damaging hail, wind or rain. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using MBStorm.

| Extreme - extraordinary threat | Expected - act within an hour | Winnipeg, Manitoba

item.description:
Windstorm Warning | High Wind Effect Issued By Hydrologic Forecast Centre. |

Manitoba Transportation and Infrastructure’s Hydrologic Forecast Centre advises high winds are expected in the afternoon of August 25th. High winds may raise water levels on the lake between 0.9 - 1.5m with significant wave action expected.

| Moderate - possible threat | Expected - act within an hour | Grand Marais, Manitoba

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
